profile: The general classroom building's name was changed to Howard Phillips Hall after an Orlando businessman and entrepreneur made significant contributions to the university. Howard Phillips Hall holds more offices and departments than it does classrooms. Notably, First Year Advising and Exploration (FYAE), University Testing Center and Student Academic Resource Center (SARC) are located in the basement. These programs offer resources for students including advising, testing help and tutoring for classes. The departments of anthropology, political science and sociology are also located in Howard Phillips Hall. Additionally, more resources for students can be found in the offices of Transfer and Transition Services, Upward Bound, Global Perspectives and UCF Faculty Senate Office.
name: Howard Phillips Hall

profile:
The John T. Washington Center with its signature covered breezeway offers students and visitors shopping, dining, banking and student services. It is centrally located on UCF's main campus between the Student Union and The John C. Hitt Library. The John T. Washington Center averages 35,000 to 40,000 visitors per day. Tenants include UCF Barnes & Noble Bookstore, Chick-fil-A, UCF Card Services, FAIRWINDS Credit Union, The Spot Print & Ship Store, Addition Financial, UCF Victim Services, Skate Shop at UCF, Revamp at UCF.

Built in 1979, this 40,000 square foot building was the original Student Union. It was later named after Dr. John T. Washington, an Associate Professor of Sociology who passed away in 1983. The renaming of the structure was a tribute to his university and community accomplishments.

Address: Suites 101 to 115 Aquarius Agora Dr. Orlando, Florida 32816

profile: The Knights Helping Knights Pantry began from a class project in a first year LEAD Scholars course in 2009. UCF students wanted to create a food pantry where fellow students would have access to free necessities if they fell on hard times. This grass roots initiative strived to ensure that UCF students would not have to choose between buying text books or buying groceries. Since its inception, the Knights Helping Knights Pantry has expanded from a closet at the Student Union to its own suite located in Ferrell Commons attached to the All Knight Study facility.
name: Knight's Pantry

profile: With the help of a $3 million donation from the L3Harris Corporation to the College of Engineering & Computer Science, the L3Harris Corporation Engineering Center (HCEC) now serves as the home of the Department of Electrical Engineering & Computer Science. The HCEC occupies 75,000 square feet and includes 30 research labs for faculty and graduate students. It also features two specialized research computer-aided virtual environments (CAVEs) for virtual and augmented reality.
name: L3Harris Engineering Center

profile:
The Libra Community features six residence halls housing approximately 1000 students who are mostly in their first-year at UCF. The Libra Community is close to the Health Center, dining hall, and Recreation and Wellness Center. There are two different styles of rooms in the community, although both are four person suites with two double occupancy bedrooms that share a common bathroom.

In the center of the community is the Libra Community Center, a common area with a large screen television, used for area residential programming and student use. There is also a common kitchen area that students may use by request of the residence life staff. There are also two laundry rooms and an area for vending machines. Students can park with a student decal in the South parking garage or surface lots located near the community.

profile: Completed in 2007, the 74,250 square-feet Psychology Building is home to the psychology department and the philosophy department. The psychology department is one of the largest College of Science programs with over 2,900 majors and 650 minors. The psychology building provides a centralized structure to house the psychology department's primary responsibilities of teaching, student research, and corporate research partnerships. The building includes classrooms, a teaching laboratory, study spaces, several research laboratories, offices and academic support. In addition, the psychology building houses a clinic that focuses on behavioral approaches to therapy without prescribing medication. The clinic serves the community by providing free treatment for individuals with social phobia through the National Institute of Mental Health program.
name: Psychology Building

profile: Robinson Observatory was built in 1994 and 1995, and dedicated on April 25, 1996. Astronomy outreach, education and research has gone on at the observatory ever since. The observatory is named for one of UCF's Founders, Herbert O. Robinson, who provided much of the funds necessary for the building's construction. The efforts of the Central Florida Astronomical Society, a local amateur astronomy group, were vital in initiating the idea of a UCF campus observatory, in seeing the project to its fruition and in finding a telescope to be housed under the dome. The observatory is currently run by the Department of Physics with the help of the Astronomy Society at UCF, a campus RSO.
name: Robinson Observatory
